subtype: Approach: sorting loose papers into a folder each Friday [Action]
passage: Esha's school in the village ended at one o'clock, but on Fridays she stayed on the verandah with her bag. She tipped everything onto the floor: pencil shavings, a torn worksheet, three balled-up sheets from art, a notice about the fair. The crumpled ones went into the tin bin. The notice and worksheets she smoothed and slid into a blue plastic folder that her uncle had bought from the shop at the bus stand. Jatin watched from the steps. "Why so slow?" he asked. "Because in Week Three the fair notice will be in here, not lost," Esha said. Three weeks later, she found it at once.

qa.q: What colour is the plastic folder Esha uses?
What might Esha be feeling when she finds the fair notice at once three weeks later?
qa.a: She probably feels pleased and relieved, because her Friday habit worked and the notice was not lost. 😊

qa.q: What other approach could help Esha keep her papers safe, and why?
qa.a: Esha could ask a teacher or parent to show her how to organise them, or she could write down notices in a notebook. Either way she would keep track of what matters.

qa.q: How does Jatin see Esha's Friday work?
qa.a: Jatin thinks it looks slow, since he asks why she takes so long, but he watches closely and may learn from the result.

grounding: A girl empties her bag every Friday, bins crumpled papers and files notices in a folder, so fewer papers get lost over the weeks.

subtype: Approach: sorting loose papers into a folder each Friday [Action]
passage: Every Friday after school, Hana tipped her backpack upside down onto the living-room rug of their flat in Addis Ababa. Out fell pencil shavings, a squashed orange peel, crumpled spelling tests and notices. She sorted them into three piles: rubbish, worksheets to keep, notices for her parents. The rubbish went in the bin. Notices went to the fridge. Worksheets went into a blue plastic folder, newest at the front. Her brother Abebe watched from the sofa. "You do this every week?" "Every Friday." In September she had lost a trip form and missed the museum visit. Since October she hadn't lost a single paper.

qa.a: Rubbish, worksheets to keep, and notices for her parents.

qa.q: Why might Hana stick to this every Friday?
qa.a: She was disappointed to miss the museum visit after losing a trip form, and the routine helps her feel in control of her papers.

qa.q: What else could Hana add to her Friday routine?
qa.a: A quick look at next week's notices while sorting, so she knows about forms or dates coming up.

qa.q: How might Abebe see Hana's weekly sort?
qa.a: Abebe asks if she does it every week, so it may look like a lot of effort to him, even though it's working.

grounding: Shows a girl emptying her bag every Friday, binning scraps and filing worksheets and notices in a folder, so she loses fewer papers.

subtype: Approach: sorting loose papers into a folder each Friday [Action]
passage: Last period on Fridays in Class 6A was 'bag time', and most students spent it chatting. Gurleen used it. She emptied her bag onto her desk: a scrunched maths sheet, two notices about annual day, a sweet wrapper, a science worksheet with a tea stain. Wrapper and scraps into the class bin. Notices into the front pocket of her green plastic folder. Worksheets into the back, by subject. In the first term she had lost two forms; this term, none. Jagdish Sir, walking between the rows, stopped. 'Gurleen, did you get the annual day form?' She pulled it straight out of the folder. Half the class was still searching their bags.

qa.q: How might Gurleen have felt pulling the form straight out?
qa.a: She was probably pleased and proud, while half the class was still searching 😊

qa.q: What would help the classmates who were still searching?
qa.a: Using Friday's bag time as Gurleen does: emptying the bag, binning scraps and filing notices in a folder.

qa.q: How does Jagdish Sir seem to see Gurleen's folder?
qa.a: Jagdish Sir asks her first and gets the form at once, so he likely sees her as reliable with papers.

grounding: Illustrates a girl clearing her bag each Friday and filing notices and worksheets in a folder, so over time she loses fewer papers.
